grammarExercises.title: Topic Marker 'Ang' vs. 'Si'
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Use 'ang' before common nouns and 'si' before singular personal names to mark the topic/focus.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Topic Marker 'Ang' vs. 'Si'' (The child is eating.)?
quiz.explanation: Use 'ang' before common nouns and 'si' before singular personal names to mark the topic/focus.

grammarExercises.title: Plural Markers 'Ang mga' vs. 'Sina'
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Use 'ang mga' (pronounced 'mang-ah') for plural common nouns and 'sina' before a group of named people.

examples.tagalog: Umalis na sina Maria at Ana.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Plural Markers 'Ang mga' vs. 'Sina'' (The guests are here already.)?
options: Bawal nandito na ang mga bisita.
Sino nandito na ang mga bisita.
quiz.explanation: Use 'ang mga' (pronounced 'mang-ah') for plural common nouns and 'sina' before a group of named people.

grammarExercises.title: Actor/Possessive Marker 'Ng' vs. 'Ni'
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: 'Ng' (pronounced 'nang') marks non-focus actors, direct objects, or possession for common nouns; 'ni' does the same for personal names.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Actor/Possessive Marker 'Ng' vs. 'Ni'' (The dog ate the bread.)?
options: Bawal kinain ng aso ang tinapay.
Sino kinain ng aso ang tinapay.
quiz.explanation: 'Ng' (pronounced 'nang') marks non-focus actors, direct objects, or possession for common nouns; 'ni' does the same for personal names.

grammarExercises.title: Plural Actor/Possessive 'Ng mga' vs. 'Nina'
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Use 'ng mga' for plural common nouns and 'nina' for multiple personal names.

examples.tagalog: Binili nina Carlo at Leo ang saging.
examples.english: Carlo and Leo bought the bananas.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Plural Actor/Possessive 'Ng mga' vs. 'Nina'' (Carlo and Leo bought the bananas.)?
options: Binili nina Carlo at Leo ang saging.
Binili nina Carlo at Leo sa saging.
Bawal binili nina carlo at leo ang saging.
Sino binili nina carlo at leo ang saging.
quiz.explanation: Use 'ng mga' for plural common nouns and 'nina' for multiple personal names.

grammarExercises.title: Locative/Directional Marker 'Sa' vs. 'Kay'
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Use 'sa' for places, directions, and time, and 'kay' when directing an action to a specific person.

examples.english: I am going to the wet market.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Locative/Directional Marker 'Sa' vs. 'Kay'' (I am going to the wet market.)?
quiz.explanation: Use 'sa' for places, directions, and time, and 'kay' when directing an action to a specific person.

grammarExercises.title: Plural Directional 'Sa mga' vs. 'Kina'
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Use 'kina' before a person's name to mean 'at/to [Person]'s place' or 'to [Person and companions]'.

examples.english: I'll sleep over at Auntie's house for now.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Plural Directional 'Sa mga' vs. 'Kina'' (I'll sleep over at Auntie's house for now.)?
options: Hindi makikitulog muna ako kina tita.
Bawal makikitulog muna ako kina tita.
Sino makikitulog muna ako kina tita.
quiz.explanation: Use 'kina' before a person's name to mean 'at/to [Person]'s place' or 'to [Person and companions]'.

grammarExercises.title: Ang-Pronouns (Ako, Ikaw/Ka, Siya)
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Singular topic pronouns. 'Ikaw' is used at the start of a sentence or standalone; 'ka' is an enclitic placed after the first word.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Ang-Pronouns (Ako, Ikaw/Ka, Siya)' (Are you the new one?)?
quiz.explanation: Singular topic pronouns. 'Ikaw' is used at the start of a sentence or standalone; 'ka' is an enclitic placed after the first word.

grammarExercises.title: Plural Ang-Pronouns (Tayo, Kami, Kayo, Sila)
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: 'Tayo' includes the listener (inclusive 'we'); 'kami' excludes the listener (exclusive 'we').

examples.breakdown: Pattern: Plural Ang-Pronouns (Tayo, Kami, Kayo, Sila)

examples.english: We (not you) are leaving now, take care (you all).
examples.breakdown: Pattern: Plural Ang-Pronouns (Tayo, Kami, Kayo, Sila)

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Plural Ang-Pronouns (Tayo, Kami, Kayo, Sila)' (Come on, let's eat!)?
quiz.explanation: 'Tayo' includes the listener (inclusive 'we'); 'kami' excludes the listener (exclusive 'we').

grammarExercises.title: Ng-Pronouns (Ko, Mo, Niya)
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Used for possession after a noun or as the actor of object-focus verbs.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Ng-Pronouns (Ko, Mo, Niya)' (Where is my key?)?
quiz.explanation: Used for possession after a noun or as the actor of object-focus verbs.

grammarExercises.title: Plural Ng-Pronouns (Natin, Namin, Ninyo, Nila)
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: 'Natin' is inclusive (our/by us); 'namin' is exclusive (our/by us, excluding listener).

examples.english: This is our (all of us) country.
examples.breakdown: Pattern: Plural Ng-Pronouns (Natin, Namin, Ninyo, Nila)
Pattern: Plural Ng-Pronouns (Natin, Namin, Ninyo, Nila)

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Plural Ng-Pronouns (Natin, Namin, Ninyo, Nila)' (This is our (all of us) country.)?
quiz.explanation: 'Natin' is inclusive (our/by us); 'namin' is exclusive (our/by us, excluding listener).

grammarExercises.title: Sa-Pronouns (Akin, Iyo, Kanya)
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Expresses strong possession before a noun (with linker) or direction toward a person.

examples.tagalog: Sa akin ang bag na ito.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Sa-Pronouns (Akin, Iyo, Kanya)' (This bag is mine.)?
options: Sa akin ang bag na ito.
Sa akin sa bag na ito.
Bawal sa akin ang bag na ito.
Sino sa akin ang bag na ito.
quiz.explanation: Expresses strong possession before a noun (with linker) or direction toward a person.

grammarExercises.title: Dual Pronoun 'Kita'
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: 'Kita' replaces 'ko ikaw' when 'I' act upon 'you' (singular).

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Dual Pronoun 'Kita'' (I love you.)?
quiz.explanation: 'Kita' replaces 'ko ikaw' when 'I' act upon 'you' (singular).

grammarExercises.title: Demonstrative Pronouns (Ito, Iyan, Iyon)
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: 'Ito' (this, near speaker), 'iyan' (that, near listener), 'iyon' (that over there, far from both).

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Demonstrative Pronouns (Ito, Iyan, Iyon)' (How much is this?)?
quiz.explanation: 'Ito' (this, near speaker), 'iyan' (that, near listener), 'iyon' (that over there, far from both).

grammarExercises.title: Locative Demonstratives (Dito, Diyan, Doon)
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: 'Dito' (here), 'diyan' (there near you), 'doon' (over there). Often shifts to rito/riyan/roon after vowels.

examples.english: Pull over right here on the side!
Let's go over there to the next corner.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Locative Demonstratives (Dito, Diyan, Doon)' (Pull over right here on the side!)?
options: Hindi para po dito sa tabi!
Bawal para po dito sa tabi!
Sino para po dito sa tabi!
quiz.explanation: 'Dito' (here), 'diyan' (there near you), 'doon' (over there). Often shifts to rito/riyan/roon after vowels.

grammarExercises.title: Ng-Demonstratives (Nito, Niyan, Noon)
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Marks non-focus objects or possession for demonstratives ('of this', 'of that').

examples.english: I'd like to buy three of this, please.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Ng-Demonstratives (Nito, Niyan, Noon)' (I'd like to buy three of this, please.)?
options: Hindi pabili po ng tatlo nito.
Bawal pabili po ng tatlo nito.
Sino pabili po ng tatlo nito.
quiz.explanation: Marks non-focus objects or possession for demonstratives ('of this', 'of that').

grammarExercises.title: Polite Second-Person 'Kayo' / 'Ninyo'
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Using plural pronouns 'kayo' or 'ninyo' with 'po' shows deep respect to an older stranger.

examples.english: Where will you be getting off, Sir?

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Polite Second-Person 'Kayo' / 'Ninyo'' (Where will you be getting off, Sir?)?
options: Hindi saan po kayo bababa, manong?
Bawal saan po kayo bababa, manong?
Sino saan po kayo bababa, manong?
quiz.explanation: Using plural pronouns 'kayo' or 'ninyo' with 'po' shows deep respect to an older stranger.

grammarExercises.title: Linker '-ng' vs. 'Na'
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Connects adjectives, numbers, or demonstratives to nouns. Use '-ng' after vowels/n, and 'na' after consonants.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Linker '-ng' vs. 'Na'' (Hot pandesal)?
quiz.explanation: Connects adjectives, numbers, or demonstratives to nouns. Use '-ng' after vowels/n, and 'na' after consonants.

grammarExercises.title: Existential 'May' vs. 'Mayroon'
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Both mean 'there is/have'. 'May' goes directly before a noun/verb; 'mayroon' (often 'meron') can stand alone or precede enclitics.

examples.tagalog: May barya ka ba? — Oo, meron.
examples.english: Do you have loose change? — Yes, I do.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Existential 'May' vs. 'Mayroon'' (Do you have loose change? — Yes, I do.)?
options: May barya ka ba? — Oo, meron.
Hindi may barya ka ba? — oo, meron.
Bawal may barya ka ba? — oo, meron.
Sino may barya ka ba? — oo, meron.
quiz.explanation: Both mean 'there is/have'. 'May' goes directly before a noun/verb; 'mayroon' (often 'meron') can stand alone or precede enclitics.

grammarExercises.title: Negative Existential 'Wala'
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Means 'none', 'nothing', or 'not present'. Takes the linker '-ng' before nouns.

examples.english: I don't have an umbrella with me.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Negative Existential 'Wala'' (There are no classes tomorrow!)?
quiz.explanation: Means 'none', 'nothing', or 'not present'. Takes the linker '-ng' before nouns.

grammarExercises.title: Identification Negator 'Hindi'
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Negates verbs, adjectives, and nouns (unlike 'wala' which negates existence/possession).

examples.english: I don't know how to swim.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Identification Negator 'Hindi'' (I don't know how to swim.)?
quiz.explanation: Negates verbs, adjectives, and nouns (unlike 'wala' which negates existence/possession).

grammarExercises.title: Actor Focus '-um-' (Infinitive / Command)
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Infix '-um-' is inserted before the first vowel of the root word for basic or natural actions.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Actor Focus '-um-' (Infinitive / Command)' (Eat -> Eat now.)?
quiz.explanation: Infix '-um-' is inserted before the first vowel of the root word for basic or natural actions.

grammarExercises.title: '-um-' Completed Aspect (Past)
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: For '-um-' verbs, the completed (past) form is identical to the infinitive form.

examples.tagalog: Uminom ako ng taho kaninang umaga.
examples.english: I drank taho earlier this morning.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies ''-um-' Completed Aspect (Past)' (I drank taho earlier this morning.)?
options: Uminom ako ng taho kaninang umaga.
Uminom ako sa taho kaninsa umaga.
Bawal uminom ako ng taho kaninang umaga.
Sino uminom ako ng taho kaninang umaga.
quiz.explanation: For '-um-' verbs, the completed (past) form is identical to the infinitive form.

grammarExercises.title: '-um-' Contemplated Aspect (Future)
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Drop '-um-' and reduplicate the first syllable of the root word.

examples.tagalog: Bili -> Bibili ako ng ulam mamaya.
examples.english: Buy -> I will buy viand later.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies ''-um-' Contemplated Aspect (Future)' (Buy -> I will buy viand later.)?
options: Bili -> Bibili ako ng ulam mamaya.
Hindi bili -> bibili ako ng ulam mamaya.
Bawal bili -> bibili ako ng ulam mamaya.
Sino bili -> bibili ako ng ulam mamaya.
quiz.explanation: Drop '-um-' and reduplicate the first syllable of the root word.

grammarExercises.title: '-um-' Incompleted Aspect (Progressive)
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Reduplicate the first syllable of the root and insert '-um-' before the first vowel.

examples.tagalog: Ulan -> Umuulan na naman sa labas!
examples.english: Rain -> It is raining outside again!

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies ''-um-' Incompleted Aspect (Progressive)' (Rain -> It is raining outside again!)?
options: Ulan -> Umuulan na naman sa labas!
Hindi ulan -> umuulan na naman sa labas!
Bawal ulan -> umuulan na naman sa labas!
Sino ulan -> umuulan na naman sa labas!
quiz.explanation: Reduplicate the first syllable of the root and insert '-um-' before the first vowel.

grammarExercises.title: Actor Focus 'Mag-' (Infinitive / Command)
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Prefix 'mag-' is used for deliberate, outward, or transitive actor-focus actions.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Actor Focus 'Mag-' (Infinitive / Command)' (Let's cook adobo.)?
quiz.explanation: Prefix 'mag-' is used for deliberate, outward, or transitive actor-focus actions.

grammarExercises.title: 'Mag-' Completed Aspect ('Nag-')
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Change the 'm-' in 'mag-' to 'n-' ('nag-') for completed past actions.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies ''Mag-' Completed Aspect ('Nag-')' (I already paid via GCash.)?
options: Hindi nagbayad na ako sa gcash.
Bawal nagbayad na ako sa gcash.
Sino nagbayad na ako sa gcash.
quiz.explanation: Change the 'm-' in 'mag-' to 'n-' ('nag-') for completed past actions.

grammarExercises.title: 'Mag-' Incompleted Aspect ('Nag-' + Reduplication)
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Use 'nag-' plus the repeated first syllable of the root for ongoing actions.

examples.english: Mom is doing laundry in the backyard.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies ''Mag-' Incompleted Aspect ('Nag-' + Reduplication)' (Mom is doing laundry in the backyard.)?
options: Hindi naglalaba si nanay sa likod-bahay.
Bawal naglalaba si nanay sa likod-bahay.
Sino naglalaba si nanay sa likod-bahay.
quiz.explanation: Use 'nag-' plus the repeated first syllable of the root for ongoing actions.

grammarExercises.title: 'Mag-' Contemplated Aspect ('Mag-' + Reduplication)
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Use 'mag-' plus the repeated first syllable of the root for future actions.

examples.english: I will rest first when I get home.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies ''Mag-' Contemplated Aspect ('Mag-' + Reduplication)' (I will rest first when I get home.)?
quiz.explanation: Use 'mag-' plus the repeated first syllable of the root for future actions.

grammarExercises.title: Actor Focus 'Ma-' (Involuntary / State Verbs)
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Used for actions that happen naturally or involve bodily states (tulog, ligo, kinig).

examples.tagalog: Matulog ka na, maaga pa tayo bukas.
examples.english: Go to sleep now, we have an early start tomorrow.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Actor Focus 'Ma-' (Involuntary / State Verbs)' (Go to sleep now, we have an early start tomorrow.)?
options: Matulog ka na, maaga pa tayo bukas.
Hindi matulog ka na, maaga pa tayo bukas.
Bawal matulog ka na, maaga pa tayo bukas.
Sino matulog ka na, maaga pa tayo bukas.
quiz.explanation: Used for actions that happen naturally or involve bodily states (tulog, ligo, kinig).

grammarExercises.title: 'Ma-' Completed ('Na-') & Progressive ('Na-' + Redup)
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Change 'ma-' to 'na-' for past, and reduplicate the root's first syllable for progressive.

examples.english: I fell asleep on the jeepney!

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies ''Ma-' Completed ('Na-') & Progressive ('Na-' + Redup)' (I fell asleep on the jeepney!)?
quiz.explanation: Change 'ma-' to 'na-' for past, and reduplicate the root's first syllable for progressive.

grammarExercises.title: Actor Focus 'Mang-' (Habitual / Plural Objects)
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Often triggers nasal assimilation (m/n/ng) on the root's initial consonant (bili -> mamili).

examples.english: We will go marketing tomorrow morning.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Actor Focus 'Mang-' (Habitual / Plural Objects)' (We will go marketing tomorrow morning.)?
options: Hindi mamamalengke kami bukas ng umaga.
Bawal mamamalengke kami bukas ng umaga.
Sino mamamalengke kami bukas ng umaga.
quiz.explanation: Often triggers nasal assimilation (m/n/ng) on the root's initial consonant (bili -> mamili).

grammarExercises.title: Ability / Accidental Actor Focus 'Maka-' / 'Naka-'
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Expresses 'able to' or 'happened to' do something.

examples.english: Were you able to buy a ticket?

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Ability / Accidental Actor Focus 'Maka-' / 'Naka-'' (Were you able to buy a ticket?)?
options: Hindi nakabili ka ba ng ticket?
Bawal nakabili ka ba ng ticket?
Sino nakabili ka ba ng ticket?
quiz.explanation: Expresses 'able to' or 'happened to' do something.

grammarExercises.title: Stative Prefix 'Naka-' (Wearing / Posture)
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Describes what someone is wearing or their current physical state/position.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Stative Prefix 'Naka-' (Wearing / Posture)' (I am already in uniform.)?
quiz.explanation: Describes what someone is wearing or their current physical state/position.

grammarExercises.title: Recent Past Prefix 'Ka-' + Reduplication
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Expresses an action that 'just happened' moments ago. Actor takes 'ng' or 'ko/mo'.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Recent Past Prefix 'Ka-' + Reduplication' (I just ate.)?
quiz.explanation: Expresses an action that 'just happened' moments ago. Actor takes 'ng' or 'ko/mo'.

grammarExercises.title: Social / Participatory Prefix 'Maki-' / 'Naki-'
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Used to politely ask to join in or use something belonging to others.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Social / Participatory Prefix 'Maki-' / 'Naki-'' (Excuse me (passing through).)?
quiz.explanation: Used to politely ask to join in or use something belonging to others.

grammarExercises.title: Reciprocal Prefix 'Mag- -an'
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Shows two or more actors doing an action to or with each other.

examples.english: We chatted with each other while having coffee.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Reciprocal Prefix 'Mag- -an'' (We chatted with each other while having coffee.)?
quiz.explanation: Shows two or more actors doing an action to or with each other.

grammarExercises.title: Pseudo-Verbs 'Gusto' and 'Ayaw'
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Expresses 'want/like' and 'don't want/dislike'. The actor takes 'ng/ko/mo' and the object takes 'ang/ng'.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Pseudo-Verbs 'Gusto' and 'Ayaw'' (I want halo-halo.)?
quiz.explanation: Expresses 'want/like' and 'don't want/dislike'. The actor takes 'ng/ko/mo' and the object takes 'ang/ng'.

grammarExercises.title: Pseudo-Verb 'Kailangan' (Need)
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Expresses necessity. Followed by a linker when paired with another verb.

examples.english: I need to buy mobile load before leaving.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Pseudo-Verb 'Kailangan' (Need)' (I need to buy mobile load before leaving.)?
options: Hindi kailangan kong mag-load bago umalis.
Bawal kailangan kong mag-load bago umalis.
Sino kailangan kong mag-load bago umalis.
quiz.explanation: Expresses necessity. Followed by a linker when paired with another verb.

grammarExercises.title: Pseudo-Verbs 'Pwede' and 'Bawal'
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: 'Pwede' means allowed/possible; 'bawal' means prohibited/forbidden.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Pseudo-Verbs 'Pwede' and 'Bawal'' (Is GCash accepted here?)?
quiz.explanation: 'Pwede' means allowed/possible; 'bawal' means prohibited/forbidden.

grammarExercises.title: Pseudo-Verb 'Dapat' (Should / Must)
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Expresses obligation or what ought to be done.

examples.tagalog: Dapat magdala ka ng payong kasi maulap.
examples.english: You should bring an umbrella because it's cloudy.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Pseudo-Verb 'Dapat' (Should / Must)' (You should bring an umbrella because it's cloudy.)?
options: Dapat magdala ka ng payong kasi maulap.
Hindi dapat magdala ka ng payong kasi maulap.
Bawal dapat magdala ka ng payong kasi maulap.
Sino dapat magdala ka ng payong kasi maulap.
quiz.explanation: Expresses obligation or what ought to be done.

grammarExercises.title: Object Focus '-in' (Infinitive / Command)
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Suffix '-in' (or '-hin' after vowels) puts the spotlight on the specific object being acted upon.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Object Focus '-in' (Infinitive / Command)' (Eat the pancit now.)?
options: Bawal kainin mo na ang pansit.
Sino kainin mo na ang pansit.
quiz.explanation: Suffix '-in' (or '-hin' after vowels) puts the spotlight on the specific object being acted upon.

grammarExercises.title: '-in' Completed Aspect (Infix '-in-')
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Drop the suffix '-in' and insert '-in-' before the first vowel of the root (or 'ni-' before l/r/w/y).

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies ''-in' Completed Aspect (Infix '-in-')' (The cat ate the fish.)?
options: Bawal kinain ng pusa ang isda.
Sino kinain ng pusa ang isda.
quiz.explanation: Drop the suffix '-in' and insert '-in-' before the first vowel of the root (or 'ni-' before l/r/w/y).

grammarExercises.title: '-in' Incompleted Aspect ('-in-' + Redup)
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Reduplicate the first syllable and insert '-in-' for ongoing object-focused actions.

examples.tagalog: Binabasa ko pa ang message niya.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies ''-in' Incompleted Aspect ('-in-' + Redup)' (I am still reading his)?
options: Binabasa ko pa ang message niya.
Binabasa ko pa sa message niya.
Bawal binabasa ko pa ang message niya.
Sino binabasa ko pa ang message niya.
quiz.explanation: Reduplicate the first syllable and insert '-in-' for ongoing object-focused actions.

grammarExercises.title: '-in' Contemplated Aspect (Redup + '-in')
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Reduplicate the first syllable of the root and keep the '-in' suffix for future actions.

examples.tagalog: Bibilhin ko ang sapatos sa payday.
examples.english: I will buy the shoes on payday.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies ''-in' Contemplated Aspect (Redup + '-in')' (I will buy the shoes on payday.)?
options: Bibilhin ko ang sapatos sa payday.
Bibilhin ko sa sapatos sa payday.
Bawal bibilhin ko ang sapatos sa payday.
Sino bibilhin ko ang sapatos sa payday.
quiz.explanation: Reduplicate the first syllable of the root and keep the '-in' suffix for future actions.

grammarExercises.title: Locative / Directional Focus '-an'
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Suffix '-an' (or '-han') focuses on the location, surface, or recipient of an action.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Locative / Directional Focus '-an'' (Open the door.)?
quiz.explanation: Suffix '-an' (or '-han') focuses on the location, surface, or recipient of an action.

grammarExercises.title: '-an' Completed Aspect ('-in- ... -an')
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Combine infix '-in-' with suffix '-an' for completed locative/recipient actions.

examples.tagalog: Binigyan ako ni Lola ng aguinaldo.
examples.english: Grandma gave me a Christmas gift.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies ''-an' Completed Aspect ('-in- ... -an')' (Grandma gave me a Christmas gift.)?
options: Binigyan ako ni Lola ng aguinaldo.
Hindi binigyan ako ni lola ng aguinaldo.
Bawal binigyan ako ni lola ng aguinaldo.
Sino binigyan ako ni lola ng aguinaldo.
quiz.explanation: Combine infix '-in-' with suffix '-an' for completed locative/recipient actions.

grammarExercises.title: '-an' Progressive & Future Aspects
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Add syllable reduplication to '-in- ... -an' for progressive, and reduplication + '-an' for future.

examples.english: I will bring food to you.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies ''-an' Progressive & Future Aspects' (Manong is adding more sago.)?
options: Bawal dinadagdagan ni manong ang sago.
Sino dinadagdagan ni manong ang sago.
quiz.explanation: Add syllable reduplication to '-in- ... -an' for progressive, and reduplication + '-an' for future.

grammarExercises.title: Benefactive / Instrumental Focus 'I-'
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Prefix 'i-' focuses on an item moved away from the actor, an instrument, or something done for someone.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Benefactive / Instrumental Focus 'I-'' (Close the window.)?
quiz.explanation: Prefix 'i-' focuses on an item moved away from the actor, an instrument, or something done for someone.

grammarExercises.title: 'I-' Completed Aspect ('I- + -in-')
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Insert '-in-' into the root while keeping the 'i-' prefix.

examples.tagalog: Ibinigay ko na ang bayad sa driver.
examples.english: I already gave the fare to the driver.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies ''I-' Completed Aspect ('I- + -in-')' (I already gave the fare to the driver.)?
options: Ibinigay ko na ang bayad sa driver.
Ibinigay ko na sa bayad sa driver.
Bawal ibinigay ko na ang bayad sa driver.
Sino ibinigay ko na ang bayad sa driver.
quiz.explanation: Insert '-in-' into the root while keeping the 'i-' prefix.

grammarExercises.title: 'I-' Progressive & Future Aspects
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Reduplicate the root's first syllable with 'i- + -in-' for progressive, or 'i-' + reduplication for future.

examples.english: I am submitting the file now.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies ''I-' Progressive & Future Aspects' (I am submitting the file now.)?
options: Bawal ipinapasa ko na ang file.
Sino ipinapasa ko na ang file.
quiz.explanation: Reduplicate the root's first syllable with 'i- + -in-' for progressive, or 'i-' + reduplication for future.

grammarExercises.title: Ability / Accidental Object Focus 'Ma-' / 'Na-'
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Used when the object is specific and the actor accidentally or successfully acts on it.

examples.tagalog: Naiwan ko ang payong ko sa tricycle!
examples.english: I accidentally left my umbrella in the tricycle!

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Ability / Accidental Object Focus 'Ma-' / 'Na-'' (I accidentally left my umbrella in the tricycle!)?
options: Naiwan ko ang payong ko sa tricycle!
Naiwan ko sa payosa ko sa tricycle!
Bawal naiwan ko ang payong ko sa tricycle!
Sino naiwan ko ang payong ko sa tricycle!
quiz.explanation: Used when the object is specific and the actor accidentally or successfully acts on it.

grammarExercises.title: Ability / Accidental Locative Focus 'Ma- -an' / 'Na- -an'
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Focuses on a person or place affected accidentally or successfully.

examples.tagalog: Naabutan kami ng malakas na ulan sa daan.
examples.english: We got caught in heavy rain on the road.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Ability / Accidental Locative Focus 'Ma- -an' / 'Na- -an'' (We got caught in heavy rain on the road.)?
options: Naabutan kami ng malakas na ulan sa daan.
Hindi naabutan kami ng malakas na ulan sa daan.
Bawal naabutan kami ng malakas na ulan sa daan.
Sino naabutan kami ng malakas na ulan sa daan.
quiz.explanation: Focuses on a person or place affected accidentally or successfully.

grammarExercises.title: Causative Prefix 'Pa-' (Having Someone Do Something)
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Prefix 'pa-' expresses requesting, ordering, or letting someone perform an action.

examples.breakdown: Pattern: Causative Prefix 'Pa-' (Having Someone Do Something)

examples.english: I got a haircut at the barber.
examples.breakdown: Pattern: Causative Prefix 'Pa-' (Having Someone Do Something)

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Causative Prefix 'Pa-' (Having Someone Do Something)' (Please print this.)?
quiz.explanation: Prefix 'pa-' expresses requesting, ordering, or letting someone perform an action.

grammarExercises.title: Polite Request Prefix 'Paki-'
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Attaches to verb roots to mean 'please do [verb] for me'.

examples.tagalog: Paki-check naman kung pumasok na ang GCash.
examples.english: Please check if the GCash transfer went through.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Polite Request Prefix 'Paki-'' (Please check if the GCash transfer went through.)?
options: Paki-check naman kung pumasok na ang GCash.
Paki-check naman kusa pumasok na sa GCash.
Bawal paki-check naman kung pumasok na ang gcash.
Sino paki-check naman kung pumasok na ang gcash.
quiz.explanation: Attaches to verb roots to mean 'please do [verb] for me'.

grammarExercises.title: Benefactive 'Ipag-' (Doing for Someone)
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Focuses on the person who benefits from an action.

examples.english: I will cook sinigang for you tomorrow.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Benefactive 'Ipag-' (Doing for Someone)' (I will cook sinigang for you tomorrow.)?
options: Bawal ipagluluto kita ng sinigang bukas.
Sino ipagluluto kita ng sinigang bukas.
quiz.explanation: Focuses on the person who benefits from an action.

grammarExercises.title: Instrumental 'Ipang-' (Using a Tool)
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Focuses on the tool or money used to accomplish something.

examples.tagalog: Ipambili mo na lang ito ng merienda.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Instrumental 'Ipang-' (Using a Tool)' (Use this (money) to buy snacks.)?
options: Ipambili mo na lang ito ng merienda.
Ipambili mo na lsa ito sa merienda.
Bawal ipambili mo na lang ito ng merienda.
Sino ipambili mo na lang ito ng merienda.
quiz.explanation: Focuses on the tool or money used to accomplish something.

grammarExercises.title: Choosing Actor Focus vs. Object Focus
grammarExercises.tagalogTitle: Paksa #57: Choosing Actor Focus vs. Object Focus
grammarExercises.topic: Choosing Actor Focus vs. Object Focus
grammarExercises.formula: Choosing Actor Focus vs. Object Focus
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Use Actor Focus ('ng' object) for indefinite/general objects; use Object Focus ('ang' object) for specific/definite objects.

examples.tagalog: Bumili ako ng kape. (a coffee) vs. Binili ko ang kape. (the specific coffee)
examples.english: I bought some coffee. vs. I bought the coffee.
examples.breakdown: Pattern: Choosing Actor Focus vs. Object Focus

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Choosing Actor Focus vs. Object Focus' (I bought some coffee. vs. I bought the coffee.)?
options: Bumili ako ng kape. (a coffee) vs. Binili ko ang kape. (the specific coffee)
Bumili ako sa kape. (a coffee) vs. Binili ko sa kape. (the specific coffee)
Bawal bumili ako ng kape. (a coffee) vs. binili ko ang kape. (the specific coffee)
Sino bumili ako ng kape. (a coffee) vs. binili ko ang kape. (the specific coffee)
quiz.explanation: Use Actor Focus ('ng' object) for indefinite/general objects; use Object Focus ('ang' object) for specific/definite objects.

grammarExercises.title: Imperative Softening with 'Nga'
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Commands in Tagalog often sound abrupt without 'nga' or 'po'.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Imperative Softening with 'Nga'' (Please have a seat first.)?
quiz.explanation: Commands in Tagalog often sound abrupt without 'nga' or 'po'.

grammarExercises.title: Negative Commands with 'Huwag' (Wag)
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Use 'huwag' (colloquial 'wag') + infinitive verb to say 'Don't...'. Enclitics move before the verb!

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Negative Commands with 'Huwag' (Wag)' (Don't worry.)?
quiz.explanation: Use 'huwag' (colloquial 'wag') + infinitive verb to say 'Don't...'. Enclitics move before the verb!

grammarExercises.title: Hortative 'Tara' and 'Tayo Na'
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: 'Tara' (let's go) and 'tayo na' (let's go now) invite the listener to move together.

examples.tagalog: Tara na, baka ma-traffic pa tayo sa EDSA!
examples.english: Let's go now, or we might get stuck in EDSA traffic!

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Hortative 'Tara' and 'Tayo Na'' (Let's go now, or we might get stuck in EDSA traffic!)?
options: Tara na, baka ma-traffic pa tayo sa EDSA!
Hindi tara na, baka ma-traffic pa tayo sa edsa!
Bawal tara na, baka ma-traffic pa tayo sa edsa!
Sino tara na, baka ma-traffic pa tayo sa edsa!
quiz.explanation: 'Tara' (let's go) and 'tayo na' (let's go now) invite the listener to move together.

grammarExercises.title: Respect Particle 'Po' and 'Opo'
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: 'Po' is inserted into sentences to show respect to elders or strangers; 'opo' means 'yes (with respect)'.

examples.tagalog: Opo, nandito na po ako sa gate.
examples.english: Yes, I am already here at the gate.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Respect Particle 'Po' and 'Opo'' (Thank you!)?
quiz.explanation: 'Po' is inserted into sentences to show respect to elders or strangers; 'opo' means 'yes (with respect)'.

grammarExercises.title: Informal Respect 'Ho' and 'Oho'
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Slightly softer/less formal than 'po', commonly used in Southern Tagalog or with familiar elders.

examples.english: Yes, Auntie, I'm about to eat.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Informal Respect 'Ho' and 'Oho'' (Please come in!)?
quiz.explanation: Slightly softer/less formal than 'po', commonly used in Southern Tagalog or with familiar elders.

grammarExercises.title: Change-of-State Particle 'Na'
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Means 'already' or 'now', indicating a new state or completed transition.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Change-of-State Particle 'Na'' (I have already eaten.)?
quiz.explanation: Means 'already' or 'now', indicating a new state or completed transition.

grammarExercises.title: Continuation Particle 'Pa'
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Means 'still' or 'yet' (with negatives) or 'more/else'.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Continuation Particle 'Pa'' (The rider isn't here yet.)?
quiz.explanation: Means 'still' or 'yet' (with negatives) or 'more/else'.

grammarExercises.title: Question Particle 'Ba'
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Turns a statement into a yes/no question. Placed after the first word or monosyllabic pronoun.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Question Particle 'Ba'' (Are you finished already?)?
quiz.explanation: Turns a statement into a yes/no question. Placed after the first word or monosyllabic pronoun.

grammarExercises.title: Limiting Particle 'Lang' (Lamang)
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Means 'only', 'just', or softens a request to make it feel small and easy.

examples.english: Right here on the side only.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Limiting Particle 'Lang' (Lamang)' (Just a moment, please.)?
quiz.explanation: Means 'only', 'just', or softens a request to make it feel small and easy.

grammarExercises.title: Confirmation / Emphasis Particle 'Nga'
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Means 'indeed', 'really', or politely softens a request.

examples.english: Let me take a look at that.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Confirmation / Emphasis Particle 'Nga'' (Yes, indeed!)?
quiz.explanation: Means 'indeed', 'really', or politely softens a request.

grammarExercises.title: Contrast / Softening Particle 'Naman'
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Expresses gentle contrast ('on the other hand', 'this time') or polite appeal.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Contrast / Softening Particle 'Naman'' (Your turn to sing!)?
quiz.explanation: Expresses gentle contrast ('on the other hand', 'this time') or polite appeal.

grammarExercises.title: Realization Particle 'Pala'
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Expresses sudden realization, surprise, or remembering something ('oh, so...').

examples.english: Oh, there's no class today after all.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Realization Particle 'Pala'' (Oh, it's you!)?
quiz.explanation: Expresses sudden realization, surprise, or remembering something ('oh, so...').

grammarExercises.title: Sequence / Priority Particle 'Muna'
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Means 'first', 'for now', or 'before doing anything else'.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Sequence / Priority Particle 'Muna'' (Let's eat first before studying.)?
options: Hindi kain muna tayo bago mag-aral.
Bawal kain muna tayo bago mag-aral.
Sino kain muna tayo bago mag-aral.
quiz.explanation: Means 'first', 'for now', or 'before doing anything else'.

grammarExercises.title: Addition Particle 'Din' / 'Rin'
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Means 'also' or 'too'. Use 'rin' after vowels/w/y and 'din' after consonants.

examples.english: Their bibingka is delicious as well.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Addition Particle 'Din' / 'Rin'' (Me too!)?
quiz.explanation: Means 'also' or 'too'. Use 'rin' after vowels/w/y and 'din' after consonants.

grammarExercises.title: Uncertainty Particle 'Kaya'
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Expresses wondering or speculation ('I wonder if...', 'perhaps').

examples.english: I wonder if the bank is open today?

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Uncertainty Particle 'Kaya'' (I wonder if the bank is open today?)?
options: Bawal bukas kaya ang bangko ngayon?
Sino bukas kaya ang bangko ngayon?
quiz.explanation: Expresses wondering or speculation ('I wonder if...', 'perhaps').

grammarExercises.title: Reported Speech Particle 'Daw' / 'Raw'
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Means 'according to someone' or 'they said'. 'Raw' follows vowels; 'daw' follows consonants.

examples.english: They say there's a typhoon tomorrow.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Reported Speech Particle 'Daw' / 'Raw'' (They say there's a typhoon tomorrow.)?
quiz.explanation: Means 'according to someone' or 'they said'. 'Raw' follows vowels; 'daw' follows consonants.

grammarExercises.title: Reason / Explanation Particle 'Kasi'
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Means 'because' (colloquial). Often placed right after the first word of the clause.

examples.tagalog: Late ako kasi na-traffic sa Ortigas.
examples.english: I'm late because I got stuck in Ortigas traffic.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Reason / Explanation Particle 'Kasi'' (I'm late because I got stuck in Ortigas traffic.)?
options: Late ako kasi na-traffic sa Ortigas.
Hindi late ako kasi na-traffic sa ortigas.
Bawal late ako kasi na-traffic sa ortigas.
Sino late ako kasi na-traffic sa ortigas.
quiz.explanation: Means 'because' (colloquial). Often placed right after the first word of the clause.

grammarExercises.title: Golden Rule of Enclitic Ordering
grammarExercises.tagalogTitle: Paksa #75: Golden Rule of Enclitic Ordering
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Monosyllabic pronouns (ka, ko, mo) come first, followed by 'na/pa', then 'ba', 'din/rin', 'lang', 'naman', 'po'.

examples.english: Have you given it already, Sir
examples.breakdown: Pattern: Golden Rule of Enclitic Ordering

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Golden Rule of Enclitic Ordering' (Have you given it already, Sir)?
options: Hindi naibigay mo na ba po?
Bawal naibigay mo na ba po?
Sino naibigay mo na ba po?
quiz.explanation: Monosyllabic pronouns (ka, ko, mo) come first, followed by 'na/pa', then 'ba', 'din/rin', 'lang', 'naman', 'po'.

grammarExercises.title: 'Ma-' Adjectives (Descriptive Quality)
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Prefix 'ma-' + root forms common adjectives (masarap = delicious, mainit = hot).

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies ''Ma-' Adjectives (Descriptive Quality)' (Grandma's sinigang is delicious.)?
options: Bawal masarap ang sinigang ni lola.
Sino masarap ang sinigang ni lola.
quiz.explanation: Prefix 'ma-' + root forms common adjectives (masarap = delicious, mainit = hot).

grammarExercises.title: Pluralizing 'Ma-' Adjectives
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Reduplicate the first syllable of the root to describe plural nouns.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Pluralizing 'Ma-' Adjectives' (Our neighbors are kind.)?
options: Bawal mababait ang mga kapitbahay namin.
Sino mababait ang mga kapitbahay namin.
quiz.explanation: Reduplicate the first syllable of the root to describe plural nouns.

grammarExercises.title: Exclamatory 'Ang' + Adjective Root
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Drop 'ma-' and put 'ang' before the root to exclaim 'How [adjective]!'

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Exclamatory 'Ang' + Adjective Root' (How delicious this is!)?
quiz.explanation: Drop 'ma-' and put 'ang' before the root to exclaim 'How [adjective]!'

grammarExercises.title: Superlative 'Pinaka-'
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Attach 'pinaka-' to the full adjective to mean 'the most [adjective]'.

examples.tagalog: Ito ang pinakamasarap na halo-halo sa bayan.
examples.english: This is the most delicious halo-halo in town.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Superlative 'Pinaka-'' (This is the most delicious halo-halo in town.)?
options: Ito ang pinakamasarap na halo-halo sa bayan.
Ito sa pinakamasarap na halo-halo sa bayan.
Bawal ito ang pinakamasarap na halo-halo sa bayan.
Sino ito ang pinakamasarap na halo-halo sa bayan.
quiz.explanation: Attach 'pinaka-' to the full adjective to mean 'the most [adjective]'.

grammarExercises.title: Comparative 'Mas ... Kaysa Sa'
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Use 'mas' before the adjective and 'kaysa sa' (than) to compare two things.

examples.tagalog: Mas malamig sa Tagaytay kaysa sa Maynila.
examples.english: It is colder in Tagaytay than in Manila.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Comparative 'Mas ... Kaysa Sa'' (It is colder in Tagaytay than in Manila.)?
options: Mas malamig sa Tagaytay kaysa sa Maynila.
Hindi mas malamig sa tagaytay kaysa sa maynila.
Bawal mas malamig sa tagaytay kaysa sa maynila.
Sino mas malamig sa tagaytay kaysa sa maynila.
quiz.explanation: Use 'mas' before the adjective and 'kaysa sa' (than) to compare two things.

grammarExercises.title: Interrogative 'Ano' (What) & 'Anu-ano'
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: 'Ano' asks 'what' (singular); reduplicated 'anu-ano' asks 'what things' (plural).

examples.english: What are the things we will buy?

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Interrogative 'Ano' (What) & 'Anu-ano'' (What time is it?)?
quiz.explanation: 'Ano' asks 'what' (singular); reduplicated 'anu-ano' asks 'what things' (plural).

grammarExercises.title: Interrogative 'Sino' (Who) & 'Sinu-sino'
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: 'Sino' asks 'who'; 'sinu-sino' asks 'who all' (plural).

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Interrogative 'Sino' (Who) & 'Sinu-sino'' (Who is with you?)?
quiz.explanation: 'Sino' asks 'who'; 'sinu-sino' asks 'who all' (plural).

grammarExercises.title: Interrogative 'Saan' vs. 'Nasaan' (Where)
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Use 'saan' for where an action happens/goes; use 'nasaan' to ask the static location of a person/thing.

examples.tagalog: Saan ka pupunta? vs. Nasaan ang susi ko?
examples.english: Where are you going? vs. Where is my key?

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Interrogative 'Saan' vs. 'Nasaan' (Where)' (Where are you going? vs. Where is my key?)?
options: Saan ka pupunta? vs. Nasaan ang susi ko?
Saan ka pupunta? vs. Nasaan sa susi ko?
Bawal saan ka pupunta? vs. nasaan ang susi ko?
Sino saan ka pupunta? vs. nasaan ang susi ko?
quiz.explanation: Use 'saan' for where an action happens/goes; use 'nasaan' to ask the static location of a person/thing.

grammarExercises.title: Interrogative 'Kailan' (When)
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Asks about dates, days, or future/past times.

examples.english: When are you going home to the province?

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Interrogative 'Kailan' (When)' (When is payday?)?
quiz.explanation: Asks about dates, days, or future/past times.

grammarExercises.title: Interrogative 'Bakit' (Why) & 'Kasi / Dahil'
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: 'Bakit' asks 'why'; answer with 'kasi' (conversational) or 'dahil' (formal/written).

examples.tagalog: Bakit ka nagmamadali? — Kasi mahuhuli na ako sa klase.
examples.english: Why are you rushing? — Because I'm going to be late for class.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Interrogative 'Bakit' (Why) & 'Kasi / Dahil'' (Why are you rushing? — Because I'm going to be late for class.)?
options: Bakit ka nagmamadali? — Kasi mahuhuli na ako sa klase.
Hindi bakit ka nagmamadali? — kasi mahuhuli na ako sa klase.
Bawal bakit ka nagmamadali? — kasi mahuhuli na ako sa klase.
Sino bakit ka nagmamadali? — kasi mahuhuli na ako sa klase.
quiz.explanation: 'Bakit' asks 'why'; answer with 'kasi' (conversational) or 'dahil' (formal/written).

grammarExercises.title: Interrogative 'Paano' (How)
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Asks for the manner or method of doing something.

examples.tagalog: Paano pumunta sa SM Megamall mula dito?
examples.english: How do I get to SM Megamall from here?

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Interrogative 'Paano' (How)' (How do I get to SM Megamall from here?)?
options: Paano pumunta sa SM Megamall mula dito?
Hindi paano pumunta sa sm megamall mula dito?
Bawal paano pumunta sa sm megamall mula dito?
Sino paano pumunta sa sm megamall mula dito?
quiz.explanation: Asks for the manner or method of doing something.

grammarExercises.title: Interrogative 'Magkano' vs. 'Ilan'
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: 'Magkano' asks 'how much (price)'; 'ilan' asks 'how many (count)'.

examples.english: How many of you are riding?

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Interrogative 'Magkano' vs. 'Ilan'' (How much is one kilo?)?
quiz.explanation: 'Magkano' asks 'how much (price)'; 'ilan' asks 'how many (count)'.

grammarExercises.title: Native Tagalog Numbers (Isa, Dalawa, Tatlo...)
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Used for counting objects, people, and general quantities (with linker '-ng' / 'na').

examples.tagalog: Dalawang order ng lugaw at tatlong tokwa.
examples.english: Two orders of congee and three fried tofu.
examples.breakdown: Pattern: Native Tagalog Numbers (Isa, Dalawa, Tatlo...)

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Native Tagalog Numbers (Isa, Dalawa, Tatlo...)' (Two orders of congee and three fried tofu.)?
options: Dalawang order ng lugaw at tatlong tokwa.
Dalawsa order sa lugaw at tatlosa tokwa.
Bawal dalawang order ng lugaw at tatlong tokwa.
Sino dalawang order ng lugaw at tatlong tokwa.
quiz.explanation: Used for counting objects, people, and general quantities (with linker '-ng' / 'na').

grammarExercises.title: Spanish-Derived Numbers for Money & Time
grammarExercises.tagalogTitle: Paksa #89: Spanish-Derived Numbers for Money & Time
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Filipinos use Spanish-derived numbers (bente, singkwenta, alas-tres) for prices and clock time.

examples.breakdown: Pattern: Spanish-Derived Numbers for Money & Time
Pattern: Spanish-Derived Numbers for Money & Time

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Spanish-Derived Numbers for Money & Time' (Fifty pesos only.)?
quiz.explanation: Filipinos use Spanish-derived numbers (bente, singkwenta, alas-tres) for prices and clock time.

grammarExercises.title: Telling Time with 'Alas-' and 'Y Media'
grammarExercises.tagalogTitle: Paksa #90: Telling Time with 'Alas-' and 'Y Media'
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Prefix 'alas-' before hours (except 'ala-una' for 1:00) and 'y media' for :30.

examples.breakdown: Pattern: Telling Time with 'Alas-' and 'Y Media'

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Telling Time with 'Alas-' and 'Y Media'' (1:30 in the afternoon.)?
options: Hindi ala-una y media ng hapon.
Bawal ala-una y media ng hapon.
Sino ala-una y media ng hapon.
quiz.explanation: Prefix 'alas-' before hours (except 'ala-una' for 1:00) and 'y media' for :30.

grammarExercises.title: Parts of the Day (Umaga, Tanghali, Hapon, Gabi)
grammarExercises.topic: Parts of the Day (Umaga, Tanghali, Hapon, Gabi)
grammarExercises.formula: Parts of the Day (Umaga, Tanghali, Hapon, Gabi)
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Used with 'ng' for recurring times or 'sa' for upcoming times.

examples.breakdown: Pattern: Parts of the Day (Umaga, Tanghali, Hapon, Gabi)
Pattern: Parts of the Day (Umaga, Tanghali, Hapon, Gabi)

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Parts of the Day (Umaga, Tanghali, Hapon, Gabi)' (Good morning!)?
quiz.explanation: Used with 'ng' for recurring times or 'sa' for upcoming times.

grammarExercises.title: Past Time Marker 'Noong' / 'Nung'
grammarExercises.detailedExplanation: Marks completed past dates, days, or events ('last...' or 'when...').

examples.tagalog: Nung Linggo, nagsimba kami sa Quiapo.
examples.english: Last Sunday, we attended Mass in Quiapo.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly applies 'Past Time Marker 'Noong' / 'Nung'' (Last Sunday, we attended Mass in Quiapo.)?
